title: Negative results from a search for a new coding mechanism: m = 2 closed on both sides, flag theorems, closed routes (no new κ)
body:
Scoping note, **no new κ**: one README, six standard-library checkers and one data file under
`research/negative-results-paradigm-search/`. No existing file changes.

**Why.** Every frontier witness (7.43e-4, #285, at the time of writing) gets its saving from the same label
(index-coding) mechanism, with a per-level coding gain of about 1.003 at m ≈ 110–120. We searched for a different
mechanism that could at least double the saving exponent on both the bit and the complex side. We found none. This PR
records what we tried and why each route fails, so others need not repeat the work. It complements Swapnil Jain's
closed-ideas list and its papers P1 and P2, and notes the overlaps.

**Main new results.** Each is stated in its model; nothing here bounds integer multiplication itself.

| Side | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Complex | **m = 2 never saves for any frames in GL₄(C).** All monomial maps are free (arbitrary phases, non-Clifford, approximate-arithmetic and "y-phase" frames included), gate coefficients are arbitrary complex numbers, and gates may join registers at different frames. Exact FO certificate on Λ²C⁴. | [cert] |
| Complex | **m = 3: no torus-invariant FO certificate can exist** in characteristic ≠ 2 (Fano matroid). | [proof] |
| Complex | **m = 3, W = 2 is closed in the dilation normal form for every s ≤ 5**: window lemmas plus Gröbner-decided coefficient systems. In the full register model, inserting one free element anywhere still gives no saving. | [proof]/[cert] |
| Complex | Exact non-Clifford diagonal frames in C[y]/(y^r+1) reduce to Clifford frames plus 2^k-th roots of unity. Approximate arithmetic is legitimate but does not relax the exact group-ring identity. | [proof]/[arg] |
| Bit | **Flag theorem:** with any per-role Levi targets (invertible lower triangular, mixed or not), any rational frames and any payload field, W·m − s ≤ Σ_{up frames} (m/2 − rank A). So **m = 2 never saves**. | [proof] |
| Bit | **Theorem G₀:** the flag bound survives mid-network Levi maps, the non-abelian model where every shear is a commutator and all character bounds fail. The proof uses Sylvester rank functions on group rings of solvable quotients; a separate adversarial review found it correct. | [proof] |
| Bit | **Abelian m = 3: s ≥ 2W + 1** for every W (tight-frame lemma). | [proof] |
| Machine operations outside the frame model | Masked gates reduce to clean ancillas; clean ancillas are blocked; Fourier-duality retirement of the bit primitive is circular; multiplicative index maps obey a valuation lemma; carry-free maps are not linear-time; nonlinear controlled-shift frames keep target cost m and make a nonlinear shear cost 2. | [proof]/[arg]/[cert] |
| Coding-gap seeds | Per-session sign gauges do not rescue an isometric frame embedding of Braverman–He's PG(2,9) code: the signed incidence system is unbalanced. Cayley seeds have gap ≤ D/\|S\|. Common-frame networks with s ≤ 8 never save, for any frames. | [cert]/[proof]/[arg] |

Section 2 of the README also records earlier routes we tried and discarded on 8–9 October:
- in-class ideas on the paired-cube design: 5-pair ports, register recycling, source-assisted words, nested-chain
  modules, centre restructuring, the bridged schedule and others;
- new-primitive ideas: different-frame gates, characteristic-0 Tanner codes, small instances, centre decoders, more
  than one saved dimension per role, cover structure, cross-level schemes.

Section 3 lists what is still open: complex m = 3 at W = 2 (two or more insertions) and W = 3; bit m = 3 at small W;
the full non-abelian bit model at m = 2; non-smooth nonlinear frames in the register model; and large m, where no
construction exists but the bounds allow up to about m/2.

```sh
cd research/negative-results-paradigm-search/checks
python3 -B complex_m2_lambda2_certificate.py   # m = 2 complex certificate, < 1 s
python3 -B multiplicative_index_maps.py
python3 -B fourier_duality_f3.py
python3 -B nonlinear_frames_m1.py              # about 2 s
python3 -B flag_model_cliques.py 2             # (3: about 10 s)
python3 -B bh_sign_gauges.py
```

**Scope.**
- The packaged checkers cover the m = 2 complex certificate, the Fourier-duality identity, the multiplicative BFS,
  the nonlinear m = 1 census, the flag-model cliques and the PG(2,9) sign test.
- The flag theorem, Theorem G₀ and the m = 3 lemmas are written proofs. Their large searches (SAT, MITM,
  Gröbner) are reported, not packaged.
- Section 2's rows summarise earlier exploration notes.
